projectCategory: DSA Module 9.3: Heap Sort, Tree Sort & Non-Comparison Linear Sorting Architecture
subject: Data Structures & Algorithms in C

projects.title: Standard Heap Sort (Max-Heapify & Extraction)
projects.description: Heap Sort converts an array into a Binary Max-Heap in `O(N)` time using `heapify()`. Iteratively swaps root maximum `arr[0]` with last element `arr[i]`, shrinks heap size, and runs `heapify(0)` to restore heap property. Guarantees `O(N log N)` time and `O(1)` in-place auxiliary memory! In this project, you will build Standard Heap Sort Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Binary Max-Heap Mechanics, In-Place Heapification & Guaranteed O(N log N) Bounds
projects.exampleText: Sort array [12, 11, 13, 5, 6, 7] using Heap Sort
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Standard Heap Sort ---
Sorted Array: 5 6 7 11 12 13
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Build Heap**: Call `heapify(i)` for `i = n/2 - 1` down to 0.
2. **Extract & Sift**: Swap `arr[0]` with `arr[i]`; call `heapify(0)` on reduced heap size.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `heap_sort()`: Solves array sorting using Standard Heap Sort.

projects.title: Counting Sort (Frequency Array & Prefix Sum Stable Placement)
projects.description: Counting Sort sorts integers within a known range `0 .. K` in LINEAR `O(N + K)` time without element comparisons! 1) Count element frequencies; 2) Compute prefix sums (running totals) to determine exact output positions; 3) Place elements backwards into output array to preserve STABILITY. In this project, you will build Counting Sort Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Linear Time Non-Comparison Sorting, Frequency Prefix Sums & Stable Element Placement
projects.exampleText: Sort array [4, 2, 2, 8, 3, 3, 1] using Counting Sort
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Counting Sort (Linear Time Non-Comparison) ---
Sorted Array: 1 2 2 3 3 4 8
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Frequency Count**: Count occurrences of each value in `count[]` array.
2. **Prefix Sum Placement**: Convert `count[]` to cumulative indices; populate `output[]` backward for stability.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `counting_sort()`: Solves array sorting in linear time using Counting Sort.

projects.title: Radix Sort (LSD Digit-by-Digit Counting Sort)
projects.description: Radix Sort sorts integers digit-by-digit from Least Significant Digit (LSD) to Most Significant Digit (MSD). Executes STABLE Counting Sort as a subroutine on each digit position (1s, 10s, 100s...). Solves sorting in `O(D * (N + K))` linear time! In this project, you will build Radix Sort Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: LSD Radix Sorting, Digit Extraction Math & Multi-Pass Stable Subroutines
projects.exampleText: Sort 3-digit numbers using Radix Sort
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Radix Sort (LSD Digit Counting Sort) ---
Sorted 3-digit numbers [170, 45, 75, 90, 802, 24, 2, 66] in O(D * (N + K)) time.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Max Value Pass**: Find max number to determine total digit passes `D`.
2. **Digit Subroutine**: Execute stable Counting Sort on `(arr[i] / exp) % 10` for `exp = 1, 10, 100...`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `radix_sort_demo()`: Solves Radix Sort using LSD digit-by-digit passes.

projects.title: Bucket Sort (Floating Point Insertion Sort in Buckets)
projects.description: Bucket Sort divides range into N uniform buckets (e.g. `[0.0, 1.0)`). Distributes array elements into corresponding buckets `idx = N * arr[i]`, sorts each bucket individually using Insertion Sort, and concatenates buckets in `O(N)` average time! In this project, you will build Bucket Sort Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Bucket Sort Partitioning, Uniform Probability Distributions & Hybrid Bucket Concatenations
projects.exampleText: Sort floating point numbers [0.897, 0.565, 0.656, 0.1234, 0.665] using Bucket Sort
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Bucket Sort (Uniform Distribution Floats) ---
Sorted floating point values [0.897, 0.565, 0.656, 0.1234, 0.665] in O(N) average time.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Bucket Distribution**: Insert element into bucket `b[N * arr[i]]`.
2. **Bucket Sort & Concatenate**: Sort each bucket; append elements into output array.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `bucket_sort_demo()`: Solves Bucket Sort for floating point numbers.

projects.title: Min-Heap In-Place Descending Heap Sort
projects.description: While Max-Heap sorts an array in ASCENDING order, a Min-Heap sorts an array in DESCENDING order in-place! Build Min-Heap using `min_heapify()`, swap root minimum with last element, and restore min-heap property. In this project, you will build Descending Min-Heap Sort in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Min-Heap In-Place Operations, Descending Order Sorting & Dual Heap Dualities
projects.exampleText: Sort array in descending order using Min-Heap
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Min-Heap In-Place Descending Heap Sort ---
Sorted array in descending order using Min-Heap in-place.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Build Min-Heap**: Call `min_heapify()` to place smallest element at root `arr[0]`.
2. **Descending Extraction**: Swap `arr[0]` with `arr[i]`; sift down `min_heapify(0)`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `min_heap_sort_descending_demo()`: Solves Descending Heap Sort using Min-Heap.

projects.title: Binary Search Tree (BST) TreeSort
projects.description: TreeSort builds a Binary Search Tree (BST) by inserting all array elements one by one (`O(N log N)` time for balanced BST), then executes an **In-Order Traversal** (`Left → Root → Right`) to output elements in sorted order! In this project, you will build BST TreeSort Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Binary Search Tree Insertion, In-Order Traversal Properties & Tree-Based Sorting
projects.exampleText: Sort array via BST In-Order Traversal
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Binary Search Tree (BST) TreeSort ---
Sorted array via BST In-Order Traversal in O(N log N) time.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **BST Build**: Insert array items into BST.
2. **In-Order Output**: Perform in-order traversal to populate sorted array.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `bst_tree_sort_demo()`: Solves TreeSort using Binary Search Tree In-Order Traversal.

projects.title: Counting Sort with Negative Integer Range Offset
projects.description: Standard Counting Sort fails when array contains negative numbers because negative array indices are illegal in C. Find minimum value `min_val`, compute offset `range = max_val - min_val + 1`, and index frequencies using `arr[i] - min_val` in O(N + Range) time! In this project, you will build Negative Range Counting Sort in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Negative Number Offsets, Range Calculation `max - min + 1` & Dynamic Array Indexing
projects.exampleText: Sort array with negative values [-5, -10, 0, 3, -1, 5] via Counting Sort
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Counting Sort with Negative Integer Range Offset ---
Sorted array with negative values [-5, -10, 0, 3, -1, 5] using range shift offset.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Min/Max Scan**: Find `min_val` and `max_val`.
2. **Index Shift**: Count frequencies using `count[arr[i] - min_val]++`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `negative_counting_sort_demo()`: Solves Counting Sort for arrays containing negative numbers.

projects.title: Radix Sort for Fixed-Length String Arrays
projects.description: Adapt Radix Sort to sort fixed-length string arrays (e.g. 3-character strings `['cat', 'car', 'bat', 'bar']`). Run character-level Counting Sort starting from rightmost character index `L-1` down to index `0` in `O(L * N)` time! In this project, you will build String Radix Sort Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: String Radix Sort, Fixed-Length Character Indexing & ASCII Counting Subroutines
projects.exampleText: Sort fixed-length string array using Radix Sort
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Radix Sort for Fixed-Length String Arrays ---
Sorted fixed-length strings ['cat', 'car', 'bat', 'bar'] character-by-character from right to left.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Character Loop**: Loop string index `pos` from `L-1` down to `0`.
2. **ASCII Counting**: Execute stable Counting Sort on ASCII value `s[pos]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `string_radix_sort_demo()`: Solves String Radix Sort for fixed-length strings.

projects.title: Bucket Sort for Uniform Distribution Floats [0.0, 1.0)
projects.description: Demonstrate why Bucket Sort achieves linear `O(N)` time when inputs are uniformly distributed over `[0.0, 1.0)`. Calculate expected bucket load `E[bucket_size] = 1`, making Insertion Sort within each bucket take constant `O(1)` time! In this project, you will build Uniform Float Bucket Sort in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Uniformity Mathematical Proofs, O(1) Bucket Insertion Times & Distribution Sorting
projects.exampleText: Sort uniformly distributed float values in [0.0, 1.0)
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Bucket Sort for Uniform Distribution Floats [0.0, 1.0) ---
Distributed floats into N array buckets; sorted individual buckets with Insertion Sort.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Uniform Hash**: Map value `x` to bucket `floor(N * x)`.
2. **Linear Expectation**: Uniform distribution guarantees average `O(1)` bucket size.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `bucket_sort_uniform_demo()`: Solves Bucket Sort for uniform floating point arrays.

projects.title: Comparison Lower Bound Proof: Why Comparison Sorts are O(N log N)
projects.description: Demonstrate the mathematical proof of why NO comparison-based sorting algorithm can run faster than `Omega(N log N)` in worst case. A decision tree for N elements has `N!` leaves and height `h >= log2(N!) = Omega(N log N)`. Explain why non-comparison sorts bypass this bound! In this project, you will build Decision Tree Lower Bound Profiler in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Decision Tree Lower Bounds, `Omega(N log N)` Mathematical Proofs & Non-Comparison Bypass
projects.exampleText: Demonstrate decision tree comparison lower bound proof
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Comparison Lower Bound Proof: Why Comparison Sorts are Omega(N log N) ---
Decision Tree leaves N! >= 2^h implies height h >= log2(N!) = Omega(N log N).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Decision Tree Model**: Every comparison branches decision tree into 2 subtrees.
2. **Stirling Approximation**: `log2(N!) >= N log2(N) - N log2(e) = Omega(N log N)`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `comparison_lower_bound_demo()`: Demonstrates Comparison Lower Bound Proof using Decision Trees.

projects.title: MSD Radix Sort (Most Significant Digit Recursive Trie-Like Bucket Sorting)
projects.description: MSD Radix Sort processes strings or numbers starting from the Most Significant Digit (MSD) moving left to right. Partition inputs into 256 sub-buckets (like a Trie), and RECURSIVELY call MSD Radix Sort on each non-empty bucket! Ideal for variable-length strings. In this project, you will build MSD Radix Sort Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: MSD Radix Sorting, Recursive Bucket Partitions & Trie-Like String Processing
projects.exampleText: Sort variable-length strings recursively using MSD Radix Sort
projects.exampleOutput:
--- MSD Radix Sort (Most Significant Digit Trie-Like Sorting) ---
Sorted variable-length strings recursively from left to right.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **MSD Bucket Split**: Group strings by character at position `pos` into 256 buckets.
2. **Sub-Bucket Recursion**: Recurse `msd_sort(bucket, pos + 1)` on individual buckets.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `msd_radix_sort_demo()`: Solves MSD Radix Sort for variable-length strings.

projects.title: Min-Max Heap Double-Ended Priority Queue Sorter
projects.description: A Min-Max Heap supports `O(1)` access and `O(log N)` deletion of BOTH the minimum AND maximum elements simultaneously! Alternating min/max levels allow double-ended priority queue operations in `O(N log N)` time! In this project, you will build Min-Max Heap Sorter in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Min-Max Heap Structures, Alternating Level Invariants & Double-Ended Priority Queues
projects.exampleText: Extract minimum and maximum elements simultaneously using Min-Max Heap
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Min-Max Heap Double-Ended Priority Queue Sorter ---
Extracted minimum and maximum elements simultaneously from Min-Max Heap structure.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Alternating Levels**: Even depth levels store Min property; odd depth levels store Max property.
2. **Dual Extraction**: Extract min from root `arr[0]`; extract max from direct children `arr[1]` or `arr[2]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `min_max_heap_sort_demo()`: Solves Min-Max Heap Sorter.

projects.title: Smoothsort (Leonardo Heap Adaptive O(N) Sorting Algorithm)
projects.description: Smoothsort (invented by Edsger W. Dijkstra) is an adaptive variation of Heap Sort based on **Leonardo Numbers** (`L(0)=1, L(1)=1, L(n)=L(n-1)+L(n-2)+1`). Runs in `O(N log N)` worst case, but achieves linear `O(N)` time for nearly-sorted inputs while using `O(1)` memory! In this project, you will build Smoothsort Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Smoothsort Algorithm (Dijkstra), Leonardo Heap Structures & Adaptive O(N) Performance
projects.exampleText: Sort nearly-sorted array in linear O(N) time using Smoothsort
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Smoothsort (Leonardo Heap Adaptive O(N) Sorting Algorithm) ---
Sorted array in O(N) time for nearly-sorted inputs using Leonardo trees heap structure.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Leonardo Trees**: Maintain forest of heaps with sizes given by Leonardo numbers.
2. **Adaptive Sifting**: Sift down elements across Leonardo trees; achieves linear `O(N)` on sorted inputs.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `smoothsort_demo()`: Solves Smoothsort adaptive sorting algorithm.

projects.title: Bitwise Radix Sort (32-Bit Integer Bit Shifting Radix Pass)
projects.description: Speed up Radix Sort on 32-bit integers by using bitwise operators (`>>` shift and `&` mask) instead of expensive division `/` and modulo `%`! Process 8 bits per pass (Base 256): 4 passes total sort 32-bit integers in ultra-fast linear time! In this project, you will build Bitwise Radix Sort Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Bitwise Shift Radix Passes, 8-Bit Digit Masking (`0xFF`) & Division-Free Speedups
projects.exampleText: Sort 32-bit integers using 8-bit bitwise radix passes
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Bitwise Radix Sort (32-Bit Bit Shift Radix Pass) ---
Sorted 32-bit integers using 8-bit radix digit passes (4 passes total).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Bit Mask**: Extract 8-bit chunk using `digit = (arr[i] >> shift) & 0xFF`.
2. **4-Pass Sort**: Execute 4 Counting Sort passes for `shift = 0, 8, 16, 24`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `bitwise_radix_sort_demo()`: Solves Bitwise Radix Sort using 32-bit integer bit shifts.

projects.title: Counting Sort In-Place Swapping without Auxiliary Output Array
projects.description: Standard Counting Sort uses `O(N)` extra memory for `output[]`. In-Place Counting Sort uses cycle-following permutation pointers to swap elements directly inside the input array into their target buckets in `O(N + K)` time and `O(K)` memory! In this project, you will build In-Place Counting Sort in C.
projects.learningOutcome: In-Place Counting Sort, Cycle-Following Permutations & O(K) Auxiliary Memory Bounds
projects.exampleText: Execute Counting Sort in-place without auxiliary output array
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Counting Sort In-Place Swapping ---
Permuted array elements in-place using cycle-following permutation pointers without O(N) auxiliary array.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Bucket Boundaries**: Compute target range boundaries for each bucket value.
2. **Cycle Swapping**: Swap element `arr[i]` into its bucket target index; repeat until cycle closes.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `inplace_counting_sort_demo()`: Solves In-Place Counting Sort.

projects.title: Pigeonhole Sort (Key-Value Range Distribution Sorter)
projects.description: Pigeonhole Sort is suitable for sorting elements where number of elements N and range of key values K are approximately equal. Creates `range = max - min + 1` pigeonhole lists, places each element in its pigeonhole, and iterates through pigeonholes to collect elements in `O(N + Range)` time! In this project, you will build Pigeonhole Sort in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Pigeonhole Principle, Key-Value Range Distributions & O(N + Range) Sorting
projects.exampleText: Distribute elements into pigeonhole lists to sort array
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Pigeonhole Sort (Key-Value Range Distribution) ---
Sorted array elements by distributing values into pigeonholes in O(N + Range) time.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Pigeonhole Allocation**: Create array of linked list pigeonholes of size `range`.
2. **Gather Pass**: Iterate pigeonholes `0 .. range-1` and copy elements back into array.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `pigeonhole_sort_demo()`: Solves Pigeonhole Sort for key-value range distributions.

projects.title: Heap Sort Bottom-Up Heap Construction in O(N)
projects.description: Demonstrate why Floyd's Bottom-Up Heap Construction takes linear `O(N)` time while inserting N items one-by-one into a heap takes `O(N log N)`. Sum of node heights `sum(n / 2^(h+1) * h) = O(N)`! In this project, you will build Linear Heap Construction Profiler in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Floyd's Bottom-Up Heap Construction, Linear O(N) Sum of Heights Math & Heap Optimization
projects.exampleText: Build initial max heap in linear O(N) time via Floyd's algorithm
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Heap Sort Bottom-Up Heap Construction ---
Built initial max heap in linear O(N) time using Floyd's bottom-up heapify algorithm.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Height Sum Math**: `sum_{h=0}^{log N} (N / 2^(h+1)) * h <= N * sum_{h=0}^{inf} (h / 2^h) = 2 N = O(N)`.
2. **Bottom-Up Loop**: Run `heapify()` starting from last non-leaf node `n/2 - 1` down to 0.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `bottom_up_heapify_demo()`: Demonstrates Floyd's Bottom-Up Heap Construction in O(N) time.

projects.title: Radix Sort for 64-Bit Floating Point Numbers (IEEE 754 Bit Conversion)
projects.description: Radix Sort on floating point numbers requires handling IEEE 754 floating point bit representation: negative floats have flipped sign bits. Transform float bits into unsigned integers using bitwise flips, run Radix Sort, and un-flip bits in `O(N)` time! In this project, you will build Floating Point Radix Sort in C.
projects.learningOutcome: IEEE 754 Floating Point Bit Conversions, Sign Bit Flipping Tricks & Float Radix Passes
projects.exampleText: Sort 64-bit IEEE 754 floating point numbers in linear O(N) time
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Radix Sort for 64-Bit Floating Point Numbers ---
Converted IEEE 754 float bitwise representation to unsigned integers to sort floats in linear time.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Float to Int Mask**: If sign bit set, flip ALL bits; else flip ONLY sign bit.
2. **Radix Pass & Unflip**: Run standard 64-bit Radix Sort; reverse bit flip transformation.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `float_radix_sort_demo()`: Solves Radix Sort for 64-Bit Floating Point Numbers.

projects.title: Bucket Sort with Dynamic Resizable Vector Buckets
projects.description: Implement Bucket Sort using dynamically resizing vector structures in C to handle non-uniform distributions safely without buffer overflows. Dynamically reallocates bucket capacities as elements arrive in `O(N)` average time! In this project, you will build Resizable Vector Bucket Sort in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Dynamic Resizable Buckets, Buffer Overflow Protection & Non-Uniform Distribution Handling
projects.exampleText: Sort non-uniform inputs using dynamically resizable vector buckets
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Bucket Sort with Dynamic Resizable Vector Buckets ---
Distributed elements into dynamically resizing memory buckets; sorted each bucket independently.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Dynamic Bucket Struct**: Maintain `capacity`, `size`, and `data*` pointer per bucket.
2. **Dynamic Realloc**: Double bucket capacity upon reaching full size.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `vector_bucket_sort_demo()`: Solves Bucket Sort with dynamically resizable vector buckets.

projects.title: Hybrid Heap-Insertion Sort for Small Suffix Subarrays
projects.description: Optimize HeapSort runtime overhead on small arrays by switching to Insertion Sort when remaining heap size `i <= 16`. Insertion Sort takes advantage of CPU L1 cache locality for small subfiles! In this project, you will build Hybrid Heap-Insertion Sorter in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Hybrid Heap-Insertion Strategy, Cache Line Optimization & Small Heap Cutoffs
projects.exampleText: Switch from HeapSort to InsertionSort for suffix subarrays N <= 16
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Hybrid Heap-Insertion Sort for Small Suffix Subarrays ---
Switched from HeapSort to InsertionSort for small suffix subfiles.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Heap Subtree Cutoff**: Run HeapSort until active heap size `n_curr <= 16`.
2. **Insertion Sort Finish**: Execute Insertion Sort on remaining elements.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `hybrid_heap_insertion_demo()`: Solves Hybrid Heap-Insertion Sort.

projects.title: Ultra-Fast 256-Radix (Base 256) Integer Sorting Engine
projects.description: Industrial high-speed sorting engines use Base 256 (8 bits per digit pass) to sort 32-bit integers in EXACTLY 4 passes! Uses 256-element frequency count tables, achieving 10x speedup over standard comparison sorts. In this project, you will build 256-Radix Integer Sorting Engine in C.

projects.logicExplanation:
1. **256 Frequency Table**: Maintain `count[4][256]` array for all 4 byte positions in single pass.
2. **4 Byte Sweeps**: Reconstruct output array using 4 consecutive byte index passes.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `radix_256_engine_demo()`: Implements Ultra-Fast 256-Radix Integer Sorting Engine.

projects.title: Cache-Oblivious Funnelsort Kernel
projects.description: Cache-Oblivious Funnelsort achieves optimal I/O memory transfers `O((N / B) * log_{M / B}(N / B))` across ALL levels of CPU cache hierarchy without knowing cache size M or block size B! In this project, you will build Funnelsort Kernel in C.

projects.title: Parallel Multi-Threaded Radix Pass Sorter
projects.description: Accelerate Radix Sort over multi-core processors by executing OpenMP parallel thread sweeps across array chunks, accumulating parallel histogram counts in `O(N / Core)` time! In this project, you will build Parallel Radix Sorter in C.
projects.learningOutcome: OpenMP Parallel Radix Passes, Multi-Core Histogram Sweeps & Thread-Local Bucket Offsets

2. **Prefix Sum Merger**: Merge local histograms into global offset table to place items in parallel.

projects.title: High-Throughput Memory-Mapped Real-Time Stream Sorter
projects.description: High-frequency streaming analytics engines sort 20,000,000 incoming telemetry records per second by executing Radix Sort directly over memory-mapped shared RAM buffers (`mmap`). In this project, you will build Real-Time Stream Sorter Kernel in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Memory-Mapped Radix Buffers, 20M Stream Sorters & Zero-Copy Linear Sorting
